title: Serving Runtime: Architecture, Kernel Scheduling, Profiling Playbook and Benchmarks
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates the serving runtime architecture, kernel-scheduling strategy, profiling playbook, benchmarking suite, recent release notes, known issues, and runbooks that the Serving Runtime team maintains. It is intended as the canonical reference for engineers operating and improving Redwood’s inference runtime (hosted, dedicated, and private deployments).

Intended audience:
- Serving runtime engineers
- SREs and capacity planners
- Model-onboarding and quantization engineers
- Performance and benchmarking contributors

Sections:
1) High-level architecture overview
2) Kernel scheduling model and config reference
3) Profiling playbook (how-to)
4) Benchmarking suite and test matrix
5) Recent release notes (summary)
6) Known issues and mitigations
7) Runbooks and incident response procedures
8) Team wiki links, ownership and triage flow

---

1) High-level architecture overview
Purpose: describe runtime components, responsibilities, and failure domains.

Components:
- Front-proxy / API layer: authenticates requests and enforces quotas. Routes requests to appropriate runtime pool (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Router & Policy layer: selects model variant, region, and fallback policy based on request metadata and SLOs.
- Worker nodes (inference runtime): GPU processes that load models, manage KV cache, and execute token generation.
- Scheduler service: global coordinator for job placement and kernel scheduling hints.
- Cache layer: shared prefix/KV cache for hot prompts and embeddings.
- Telemetry & Observability: metrics, traces, and profiles forwarded to metrics backend and tracing collector.

Service boundaries and SLOs (service-level summary):
- P95 completion latency target: 350ms for short-text workloads (<= 128 tokens) on hosted p2 instances.
- Availability SLO: 99.95% per region for Dedicated pools.
- Error budget policy: 12.5% of incident budget reserved for kernel regressions; automatically triggers canary rollback if spike > 3x baseline.

Operational ownership:
- Runtime core: eng-serving-runtime (primary)
- Scheduler & autoscaler: eng-platform (secondary)
- Observability & alerts: eng-sre (oncall)

---

2) Kernel scheduling model and config reference
Overview:
We run a two-tier scheduling model: local GPU-level kernel scheduler inside the worker process (micro-scheduling) and a global placement scheduler (macro-scheduling) that assigns requests to workers. Kernel scheduling is tuned per model family and quantization profile.

Goals:
- Maximize GPU utilization while preserving tail latency SLOs
- Avoid head-of-line blocking by request priority and prefix cache affinity
- Favor memory locality for KV cache reuse

Key knobs and default values (table):
| knob | purpose | default | notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| preemptive_priority_threshold | demotes batching of large requests | 4096 tokens | tokens > threshold processed with priority path |
| batch_max_tokens | upper bound per batch across requests | 32768 | tuned per-GPU (A100 80GB baseline) |
| kv_cache_locality_window_s | prefer same-worker reuse | 30 | seconds of affinity, tuned for chat workloads |
| kernel_variant | which kernel path (fast/robust) | fast_fp16 | fallbacks to robust_int8 on OOM |
| quant_profile | quantization profile tag | q4_0 | influences kernel selection and memory estimator |

Example config snippet (YAML):
```yaml
worker: 
  batch_max_tokens: 32768
  preemptive_priority_threshold: 4096
  kv_cache_locality_window_s: 30
  kernel_variant: fast_fp16
  quant_profile: q4_0
  oom_policy: fallback_to_robust
```

Kernel selection flow (simplified):
1. Model loaded with metadata (architecture, supported_kernels, quant_profiles).
2. For incoming request, compute expected token footprint (prompt + expected generation).
3. If footprint + resident_memory > mem_threshold -> select lower-memory kernel_variant (robust_int8) or reject if not allowed.
4. Consider batch composition: prefer same-architecture grouping; break batches if priority request present.

Scheduling heuristics (policy):
- Priority > SLA: routing selects hot lane with smaller batches and higher CPU cores per worker.
- Cold model loads: prefetch kernels and warm KV cache with lightweight dummy requests.
- Burst protection: maintain reserve workers (10% of pool) for spikes exceeding 2x baseline RPS.

---

3) Profiling playbook (how-to)
Purpose: capture reproducible profiling, attribute hotspots (kernel, memory copy, synchronization), and produce remediation plans.

Prerequisites:
- Profiling image: uses runtime with debug symbols build (tag: debug-profiling-2027).
- Access: must be in eng-serving-runtime or eng-sre group.
- Baseline test set: canonical prompt set (see benchmarking section).

High-level steps:
1) Reproduce workload in an isolated profiling pool. Use canary pool to prevent customer impact.
2) Collect system-level metrics: nvidia-smi sampling, iostat, and top at 1s granularity for 5 minutes.
3) Collect runtime-level telemetry: per-batch timing, kernel op traces, memcpy bytes and durations.
4) Run GPU-level profiler (Nsight Systems or CUPTI) capturing 10-30 second windows for representative requests.
5) Aggregate traces and open an analysis ticket with the perf template.

Commands (example):
- Start isolated canary pool: rctl pool create --name perf-canary --size 3 --tag profiling
- Run load generator (short workload): 
  ./perf-runner --model gpt-j-6b --profile-set small-chat --concurrency 12 --duration 120
- Collect nsys timeline: 
  nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=trace-perf-candidate nvidia_app_cmd

Profiling checklist (use and mark findings):
- [ ] Confirm whether tail latency is kernel CPU-bound (host memcpy or thread scheduling) or GPU-bound (SM utilization low/high).
- [ ] Identify expensive kernels (>30% of generation time) and record op name and histogram.
- [ ] Check for frequent small memcopies (<1KB) that indicate fragmentation or suboptimal batching.
- [ ] Validate KV cache hit rate and eviction churn.
- [ ] Confirm whether preemption or OS-level scheduling is introducing >5ms context-switch latency.

Reporting and remediation:
- Fill the performance-ticket template in Jira: PERF-<repo>-<date>. Include traces, flamegraphs, and suggested fixes (kernel rewrite, batching change, or configuration tweak).
- Suggested priority actions: bump batch_max_tokens, adjust batch composition heuristics, increase worker CPU quotas for memcpy heavy workloads, or add a specialized fast-path kernel.

---

4) Benchmarking suite and test matrix
Purpose: standardized benchmarks for capacity planning, kernel evaluation, and release gating. All benchmarks are run against the canonical harness: benchmark-runner v2.1.

Test matrix axes:
- Model family: small (1–7B), medium (7–20B), large (20B+).
- Quant profiles: fp16, q4_0, q8_0, int8_robust.
- Sequence lengths: short (<=128), medium (129–512), long (512–2048).
- Request patterns: chat (many short turns), streaming (token-by-token), batch-generate (few large requests).

Key metrics collected:
- tokens/sec (throughput)
- p50/p95/p99 latency per completion
- GPU SM utilization and memory consumption
- KV cache hit ratio
- tail_latency_99_impact_on_cost (tokens/sec vs cost)

Benchmark example command (CI):
./benchmark-runner --model gpt-7b --quant q4_0 --seq-length 128 --pattern chat --concurrency 24 --duration 600 --out results/gpt7b-q4_0-128.json

Benchmark result artifact (JSON):
- store path: s3://redwood-benchmarks/<date>/<model>-<quant>-<seq>.json
- required fields in artifact: model, quant_profile, seq_length, concurrency, tokens/sec, p50, p95, p99, sm_utilization_avg, memory_max_mb

Release gating policy:
- Major runtime releases must show >= 95% parity in p95 latency vs baseline for all representative workloads and no regression > 2% in tokens/sec.
- Kernel micro-releases are allowed to shift latency by up to 5% if they yield >10% cost savings; must be approved by perf-owner.

---

5) Recent release notes (summary)
Release: runtime-v2027.10.4 (summary)
- Kernel improvements: vectorized attention kernel "attnv2" enabled for decoder-only models, ~12% throughput improvement on medium sequences.
- Memory estimator: improved resident memory predictor to reduce OOMs during mixed workloads.
- New metrics: per-batch memcpy_time_ms and kernel_variant label.
- Bugfix: resolved intermittent stray CUDA memcpy on worker shutdown (INC-987).

Backwards compatibility notes:
- The new attnv2 kernel is enabled by default for q4_0 and fp16 on supported GPUs. Teams can opt-out via kernel_variant: robust.

---

6) Known issues and mitigations
Open issues (top priority):
- Issue: Intermittent p99 spikes for streaming workloads on A100-p2 pools (SYM-214).
  - Symptom: ~10% of requests > 1.5x normal p99 for 30–90s windows.
  - Root cause (current): kernel preemption interactions with host-side memcpy during high context-switch load.
  - Mitigation: enable per-worker memcpy_cpu_quota=0.6 and reduce concurrency for streaming lanes.
  - Owner: Diego Alvarez.

- Issue: Increased OOM rate for large context (<4096 tokens) with q8_0 profile in mixed pools (MEM-341).
  - Mitigation: recommended per-model config: batch_max_tokens=24576 and preemptive_priority_threshold=8192; schedule large-context models on dedicated nodes with higher mem_threshold.

- Issue: Profiling artifacts lost when worker restarts during trace window.
  - Mitigation: use remote nsight upload endpoint and increase profiler window to 20s.

Closed issues (last 90 days):
- INC-987 (fixed): stray CUDA memcpy on shutdown.

---

7) Runbooks and incident response procedures
High-level runbook for latency incident (p95/p99 regression):
1. Triage: verify alert in paging system (PagerDuty) and measure scope (regions, models, pools).
2. Escalate to oncall (eng-sre) then runtime-owner (eng-serving-runtime).
3. If regression isolated to kernel_variant or SKU, roll out rollback: 
   - rctl deploy set --pool <pool> --kernel_variant robust_int8 --rolling 20%
4. Start profiling capture on two affected workers (see profiling playbook). Tag traces with incident id.
5. If rollback resolves tail, keep rollback for 2 hours and schedule postmortem; if not, increase reserve-workers and enable burst-protection.

Detailed memory OOM runbook:
- Detect: OOM rate > 0.5% of requests over 5m window.
- Immediate action: set oom_policy=fallback_to_robust and move hot models to high-mem pool.
- Long-term: run memory estimator across model versions and add to model-onboarding checklist.

Runbook snippets (commands):
- Rollback kernel variant: rctl pool set --name <pool> --kernel_variant robust_int8
- Increase reserve workers: rctl pool scale --name <pool> --reserve 0.15
- Start profiler on worker: rctl worker exec --id <id> -- nsight-launch --duration 30

---

8) Team wiki links, ownership and triage flow
Primary contacts:
- Runtime lead: Ava Martinez (owner)
- Perf owner: Priya Natarajan (perf gating and benchmarks)
- SRE liaison: Ethan Park

Contributors: list is maintained in team Wiki (link internal). For code ownership see CODEOWNERS in the runtime repo.

Triage flow (summary):
1. Alert fires -> PagerDuty to eng-sre -> assign incident lead.
2. Incident lead creates incident ticket and tags eng-serving-runtime.
3. Runtime engineer runs immediate mitigations (kernel rollback, pool scaling) and starts profiling.
4. Postmortem within 72h for sev>=2 incidents; publish to confluence incident-review.

Appendix A: Perf ticket template (copy into new Jira ticket)
- Title: [PERF] <short description>
- Impacted models: <list>
- Metric regression: <p95/p99 change>
- Attachments: nsys, timelines, perf-runner output
- Suggested fixes: <short list>

Appendix B: Example configuration table
| environment | batch_max_tokens | kernel_variant | reserve_workers | notes |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| hosted-prod | 32768 | fast_fp16 | 0.10 | default hosted profile |
| dedicated-highmem | 65536 | fast_fp16 | 0.05 | for large-context customer pools |
| private-onprem | 24576 | robust_int8 | 0.15 | conservative defaults for air-gapped installs |
